Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the UniBank Holdings Third Quarter 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. As a reminder, instructions for queuing up will be given at that time. Please note this event is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to review UniBank Holdings's results for the third quarter. With me this morning are Johnathan Hale, Chief Executive Officer; Sarah Mitchell, Chief Financial Officer; David Chen, Chief Risk Officer; Lisa Patel, Chief Credit Officer; and Mike Thompson, Chief Technology Officer.

Before we begin, let me remind you that some of the statements we will be making today are forward-looking. These statements are based on current expectations and assumptions and are subject to risks and uncertainties. Please refer to our SEC filings for a discussion of these factors.

I will now turn the call over to Johnathan Hale.

Johnathan Hale:
Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. UniBank Holdings delivered excellent results in the third quarter, demonstrating the strength of our franchise and our ability to navigate a dynamic market environment.

Our key priorities for this year remain focused on:
1. Expanding our market share
2. Improving our efficiency ratio
3. Strengthening our balance sheet
4. Investing in our people
5. Driving innovation
6. Meeting our ESG goals.

Now, I'd like to provide some highlights on our overall company performance, net interest income trends, risk-weighted assets management, the macroeconomic outlook, key guidance assumptions, and technology investments. Year-to-date, we've achieved record profits with revenue growth outpacing peers, driven by robust NII expansion both year-over-year and quarter-over-quarter, alongside disciplined RWA optimization that's bolstered our capital ratios. The macro environment shows resilience with a soft landing in sight, supporting our outlook, while our tech initiatives are delivering meaningful efficiency gains. These elements position us strongly as we head into year-end.

I will now turn the call over to Sarah Mitchell to discuss our financial results in more detail.

Sarah Mitchell:
Thank you, Johnathan, and good morning. UniBank Holdings reported net income of $850 million for the third quarter, or $1.45 per diluted share. Our results reflect strong revenue growth, disciplined expense management, and a healthy credit environment.

Diving deeper into our standout performance this quarter, full-year revenue is tracking toward a record $28.7 billion, up around 14% from last year on an adjusted basis, with net income on pace for significant gains and ROTCE expanding toward 15.8%. We've returned substantial value to shareholders, including progress on a $4 billion buyback authorization and a recent dividend increase. Our balance sheet is rock-solid, with CET1 at 13.2%, up meaningfully quarter-over-quarter thanks to proactive de-risking.

Net interest income remains a cornerstone of our profitability in this high-rate world. For the quarter, NII reached $1.285 billion, up 5.2% from $1.221 billion in the second quarter and a robust 14.8% higher than $1.119 billion in the third quarter of 2023. This growth highlights our effective balance sheet management and yield capture amid deposit cost pressures and softer loan demand. Our net interest margin widened 18 basis points sequentially to 3.52%—the highest in over a decade—and 42 basis points year-over-year from 3.10%, exceeding our guided range of 3.40% to 3.50%.

Key drivers included earning asset yields rising 22 basis points to 5.38%, propelled by repricing in our $45.2 billion commercial and industrial loan portfolio, up 3% quarter-over-quarter, with yields at 6.15% from variable-rate resets linked to SOFR and prime. Consumer lending yields edged up 15 basis points to 4.85%, supported by $2.8 billion in new auto loan originations at competitive sub-6% rates. Deposit costs rose 28 basis points to 2.95%, with betas at 65% on interest-bearing deposits, but we grew non-interest-bearing deposits 4.1% to $28.4 billion, or 22% of total deposits, leveraging our UniDigital app, which added 15% more users to 4.2 million active accounts.

Average earning assets grew 1.8% to $152.3 billion, boosted by $2.1 billion in investment securities like agency MBS and short-duration corporates yielding 4.8% to 5.2%, hedged with $1.5 billion in receive-fixed swaps. Year-over-year, asset yields jumped 112 basis points, outpacing peers, as our loan mix shifted with C&I and CRE now at 58% of the portfolio. Funding costs increased 168 basis points due to higher betas at 72%, with some Midwest commercial deposit runoff, but we sold $3.2 billion in low-yield AFS securities to lift securities yields 45 basis points.

Regionally, the Southeast shone with 18% NII growth on Florida and Texas CRE demand from data centers and multifamily, averaging 6.4% yields via REIT partnerships. Midwest deposits stabilized through treasury management fee offsets up 12%, while West Coast money market accounts at 4.75% APY drew $1.1 billion inflows against fintech competition.

To sustain this, we introduced UniLock CDs gathering $4.5 billion at up to 5.1% rates, extending duration; our $10 billion swap book provides 75 basis points of margin protection through 2025; and a $18 billion C&I pipeline with 65% floating rates favors industrial and healthcare over office CRE. We guide Q4 NII to $1.30 to $1.35 billion, with NIM at 3.50% to 3.60%, assuming stable Fed funds.

Turning to risk-weighted assets management, a key part of our capital strategy under Basel III and IV, total RWAs ended the quarter at $452 billion, down 4.2% quarter-over-quarter and 7.8% year-over-year. This supports our CET1 expansion and enables strong returns to shareholders. Credit RWAs, 87% of the total at $393 billion, fell 5.1%, aided by recalibrated IRB models reducing PD 120 basis points on our $150 billion CRE book, plus $12 billion in sales and syndications of higher-risk loans. We completed $4.2 billion in CLO securitizations for 45% RWA relief.

In the Americas, 55% of credit RWAs at $216 billion declined 6.8% via CRE de-risking, cutting office exposure 15%. EMEA RWAs rose slightly to $112 billion but were hedged with CDS on energy names, dropping weights to 20%. APAC at $71 billion benefited from early output floor adoption. We've stress-tested for Basel IV's SA-CR, projecting minimal uplift, and shifted to lower-RWA green bonds and AI-scored consumer loans at 35% density.

We expect 2-3% RWA growth next year, supporting 70-80% earnings payouts.

On the macroeconomic front, the global economy is resilient, with IMF forecasting 3.2% GDP growth. U.S. GDP at 2.8% annualized in Q2 rides strong consumer spending and 3.7% unemployment, though leading indicators suggest softening. Fed terminal rate at 5.25-5.50% with 75 basis points of cuts priced in; yield curve steepening aids NII. Inflation at 3.0% CPI could face commodity risks.

North America CRE stresses persist with 20.1% office vacancies, but our 8% exposure is floating-rate heavy; consumer delinquencies stable. Europe grows slowly at 0.3% QoQ, with our NII up 12% on green bonds. APAC benefits from China's rebound and India SMB growth. These dynamics fueled our 9% NII rise to levels ahead of peers, 4% loan growth skewed to C&I, and 14% fee surge from wealth and trading.

Our GenAI risk platform cuts validation times 40%; we're repurchasing shares and hiking dividends for mid-teens ROE, while embedded finance and payments drive new revenue.

Our technology investments are transforming efficiency, with our ratio at 52.3%, down 280 basis points year-over-year and better than the 58% peer median. Over $1.2 billion invested yielded 3.2x ROI. Cloud migration at 85% slashed TCO 35% or $180 million annually, handling 1.2 million TPS. GenAI underwriting sped approvals to 4 hours, lifting volumes 15%; fraud models saved $95 million. RPA automated 65% of back-office, cutting 1,200 FTE equivalents and unit costs 31%; STP at 92% in payments.

North America efficiency at 50.1% via embedded finance; Europe 53.8% with open banking; APAC 48.5% on mobile upgrades. 2024 budget $1.4 billion targets sub-50% ratio, enhancing NPS and moats.

Finally, our full-year guidance assumes $8.10 to $8.30 adjusted EPS, 5-7% NII growth, mid-teens ROTCE. Macro: 2.2-2.5% U.S. GDP, 75-100 bps Fed cuts. Loans $1.15-1.17 trillion at 4-5% growth; deposits flat to +2%. Non-interest revenue up 6-8% on IB fees and cards. Expenses $38.5-39 billion for 56-58% ratio; provisions $4.2-4.5 billion. U.S. drives growth, with tech like BNPL pilots and ESG supporting outperformance.

We are on track to meet our financial targets for the year.

David Chen:
Thank you, Sarah. From a risk perspective, we are closely monitoring geopolitical tensions and CRE market softness. We are taking proactive steps to mitigate these risks and maintain a strong risk profile, including ongoing scenario analysis and contingency buffers.

Lisa Patel:
Good morning. Our credit quality remains strong with non-performing loans at 0.85% and net charge-offs at 0.28%. We are actively managing our loan portfolio and remain confident in our ability to navigate the current economic environment.

Operator, we are now ready to open the line for questions.

Operator:
Ladies and gentlemen, as a reminder, to ask a question, please press star then one on your telephone keypad. Our first question comes from Emily Carter with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Emily Carter:
Good morning. Can you elaborate on your Q4 NII guidance and deposit beta assumptions?

Johnathan Hale:
Thanks, Emily. As Sarah outlined, we're guiding $1.30 to $1.35 billion for Q4, with NIM 3.50-3.60%, based on stable rates and our hedging. Deposit betas should compress toward 45% as we optimize via UniLock products and digital relationships, providing resilience against MMF competition.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Robert Kline with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Robert Kline:
What is your strategy for managing RWA growth into 2025 amid Basel IV?

Sarah Mitchell:
Great question, Robert. We're targeting 2-3% growth through model refinements, securitizations like our recent CLOs, and shifts to green assets. Our early SA-CR testing shows limited uplift, and regional de-risking in CRE keeps us ahead, freeing capital for buybacks similar to leading peers.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Sophia Lee with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Sophia Lee:
How are you addressing CRE exposure in the current macro outlook?

David Chen:
Sophia, thanks. Our CRE is tightly managed at 8% of loans, with 85% floating and office under 5%. We're monitoring vacancy and cap rates closely, using forward-looking overlays and syndications to distribute risk, while favoring industrial and multifamily with strong partners.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Michael Torres with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Michael Torres:
Can you update us on technology ROI and efficiency trajectory?

Lisa Patel:
On credit tech specifically, Michael, our AI scoring has stabilized consumer metrics, but broadly, as Sarah noted, cloud and GenAI are delivering 3.2x returns, with sub-50% efficiency by 2025 via automation and APIs. This supports credit decisions and overall resilience.

Operator:
There are no further questions at this time. I'd like to turn the conference back over to Johnathan Hale for any closing remarks.

Johnathan Hale:
Thank you for your interest in UniBank Holdings. We appreciate you joining us today. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.

aspect_summary.Macroeconomic outlook and impact: Resilient global economy (IMF 3.2% GDP); US Q2 GDP 2.8%, unemployment 3.7%, 75 bps Fed cuts, 3.0% inflation, CRE office vacancies 20.1% but low 8% exposure; supported 9% NII rise, 4% loan growth, 14% fee surge.
aspect_summary.Key assumptions underlying the guidance: FY guide: $8.10-8.30 adj EPS, 5-7% NII growth, mid-teens ROTCE; assumes 2.2-2.5% US GDP, 75-100 bps Fed cuts, loans $1.15-1.17T (4-5% growth), deposits flat to +2%, non-int rev +6-8%, expenses $38.5-39B, provisions $4.2-4.5B.

aspect_summary.Overall company performance highlights: Q3 net income $850M ($1.45/share); FY revenue ~$28.7B (+14% YoY adj), ROTCE ~15.8%, CET1 13.2% (up QoQ); record YTD profits, revenue > peers, $4B buyback progress, dividend hike, efficiency gains.
